extracted.intended_audience: President and Council of Fort St. George; East India Company officials and colonial administrators in India
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and binding principles for negotiating surrender of the assignment, settling the Nabob's private debts, arranging treaties with the Nabob and Rajah, and managing repairs and water-works in the Carnatic; directed to Company representatives on the spot. Focuses on revenue application, security for payments, and preservation of civil authority while ensuring military support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit Rajah's liability to government share collected
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rajah ought to be answerable for no more than the amount of what he admits was collected by his people for the government share of the crop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not compel the Rajah to pay supposed balances or render specific accounts after the lapse of time; since he has deposited one lac of pagodas as security, surcease further demands from him on this account unless further orders are received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Rajah's deposit subject to local judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is unclear whether the deposited one lac of pagodas covers grain taken from assignees (e.g., Mr. Benfield) or what compensation has been made, local authorities are to apply the deposit consistent with principles of justice and consult the Board if difficulty arises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You on the spot should make such application of the deposit as aligns with the Board's expressed sentiments; if difficulties present themselves, suspend application and seek further orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow Rajah to repair Anicut and banks by former usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rajah should be permitted to repair the Anicut and banks of the Cavery in the same manner as had been practiced in times past.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish regulations by reference to former usage to keep banks in repair; this will be effectual and remove cause of future complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer Trichinopoly materials for repairs; obtain Nabob's permission for extraction/lease
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials from Trichinopoly are far preferable and cheaper for repairs than those from Tanjore; apply to the Nabob to permit set spots of ground on the Trichinopoly side where sand and earth may be taken, and for the Nabob to grant a lease of such spots to the Company at reasonable rent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If expedient, request the Nabob in the Company's name for permission and lease; make the lease no longer in force than while the Rajah remains punctual in payments (peshcush and reserved rent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease conditional on punctual payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any lease granted for materials/ground should remain in force only while the Rajah is punctual in payment of annual peshcush to the Nabob and the reserved rent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie continuance of lease to punctuality to remove jealousy and complaints between parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent diversion of Cavery water and represent to Nabob when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: If attempts are made to divert the Cavery into the Coleroon by contracting the current, planting long grass, or other means, represent to the Nabob in the Company's name to prevent his people from taking measures detrimental to Tanjore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Nabob, being interested in Tanjore's prosperity, is expected to prevent such measures when properly represented to him.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ skilful engineers at Rajah's expense under Company's appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend that skilful engineers appointed by the Company, and employed at the Rajah's expense, conduct necessary works on the Anicut and banks with strict attention to rights and interests of both parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This will remove probability of injury or dispute; engineers act under government of Madras and provide immediate redress without discussion between parties that might disturb harmony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrender the assignment to the Nabob while securing Company interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the Board resolves the assignment shall be surrendered to his Highness, the Company expects the Nabob to accede to arrangements necessary for common safety and to preserve Company's rights and interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use utmost endeavours to impress expediency of treaties; secure provisions ensuring contributions to military force and safeguards for Company's civil interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require Nabob soucar security of twelve lacs pagodas per annum
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nabob shall give soucar security for punctual payment, by instalments, into the Company's treasury of twelve lacs of pagodas per annum (as voluntarily proposed) until his debts with interest are discharged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also consent that equitable provisions recently made by British legislature for liquidation of those debts and future resolutions under that authority shall be carried into full force and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Bengal government determinations on security disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: If difficulty arises between his Highness and the Fort St. George government regarding responsibility of the soucar security or instalment terms, obey the orders and resolutions of the Governor-General and Council of Bengal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board trusts the Nabob will consent to abide by the supreme government's determination if such disputes occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve right to demand additional security on default
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of failure of the proposed security or default of payment, the Company reserves full right to demand additional security by assignment on his country sufficient for the purposes of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reservation protects the Company's and private creditors' interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treaties must bind parties to contribute jointly to military support
rubrics_metrics.description: Treaties should be grounded on equity: all contracting parties shall be bound to contribute jointly to the support of the military force and garrisons, as well in peace as in war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such arrangements should ensure common defence and that contributions are secure by specified districts and revenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company to settle military peace establishment
rubrics_metrics.description: The military peace establishment shall be forthwith settled and adjusted by the Company, pursuant to the authority of the late act of Parliament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because payment of troops and garrisons must be punctual, no latitude of personal assurance should be accepted; payments must be secured by specified revenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify districts/revenues to secure military/civil payments; Company power on default
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nabob and Rajah must specify particular districts and revenues for securing due and regular payment of their contributions into the Company's treasury; in case of default, the Company may enter upon and possess such districts and let them to renters (to be confirmed by the Nabob/Rajah).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Couple this with positive assurance to support their civil authority; the Company holds power to possess revenues for security but should respect civil administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate revenues during war for common defence; no commercial application
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of hostility on the Coromandel coast, whole revenues of respective territories shall be considered one common stock for defence; the Company shall refrain during the war from applying revenues to commercial purposes and shall apply the whole (except ordinary civil charges) to the war; Nabob and Rajah shall do likewise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures united defence and finance; but ascertain and set apart an indispensable sum for civil establishment beforehand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascertain and protect indispensable civil establishment sum
rubrics_metrics.description: Ascertain the sum indispensably necessary for civil establishment and hold it sacred under every emergency, setting it apart prior to applying the rest of revenues for mutual defence or war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clearing incumbrances necessarily incurred beyond ordinary war expenditure; this clarity preserves peace and financial credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company to administer aggregate revenue during war and account faithfully
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole aggregate revenue during the war shall be under the Company's application and may continue after the war as necessary to discharge burdens; the Company must produce regular accounts to other contracting parties of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision must not deprive Nabob or Rajah of substantial authority to collect revenues; if misapplication occurs, Company may take collection upon itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit Nabob's and Rajah's private troops; Company to supply extra military aid
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nabob shall agree not to maintain more troops than necessary for dignity and splendour (a number to be specified); if military aid beyond fixed establishment is required for security and collection, the Company must furnish it. The Rajah of Tanjore to have like engagements and aid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fix the number in treaty to avoid unnecessary expense while preserving honour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit renters to hold leases to term where reasonable
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to the Nabob for consent that renters who hold sundry leases may be permitted to hold them to the end of the stipulated term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Nabob refuses, do not insist as essential; instead give indemnification to renters for any loss as judged reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect natives who faithfully administered collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Natives who were put in authority over collections under the deed of assignment and proved faithful should not suffer inconvenience on account of their fidelity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It concerns the honour of the government to preserve fairness to such persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate opinions about Indian powers with prudence and discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Opinions and speculations regarding powers in India should be communicated with prudence, discretion, and as much secrecy as possible, and expressed in terms as little offensive as possible to those powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board applauds prudence in communicating suspicions, but warns against gratuitous offensive language that could harm relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use conciliation before issuing measures like Torana Chits
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuing the Torana Chits in Lord Macartney's own name can only be justified upon absolute necessity; more time and precautions of address, civility, and conciliation ought to have been used beforehand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precaution and conciliation should precede acts likely to be irksome to native rulers; omission is blameworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat private debts classes distinctly and require investigation where needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Different classes of Nabob's private debts (consolidated 1767, Cavalry Loan 1777, consolidated 1777) have differing grounds for recognition and protection; 1767 appears just and to be treated as constituted by original bonds at 10% interest, while the 1777 loans require closer scrutiny and may be less sanctioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not regard claims that improperly assert 1767 status without special instructions; for doubtful claims transmit complaints and evidence for final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit Company sanction to security for private debts without Court authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Company shall give no sanction or authority to any kind of security for payment or liquidation of Nabob's private debts (except by express authority of the Court of Directors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically refuse sanction to the loan of 1777 and similar instruments; protect the Company against being implicated in improper private securities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution rules for the twelve lacs of pagodas
rubrics_metrics.description: The twelve lacs annually received are to be applied in a prioritized manner: (1) to the growing interest on the Cavalry Loan at 12%; (2) to the growing interest on the debt of 1777 at 6% (after Nov 1781); the remainder to be equally divided — one half to the Company's debt and one half to 10% interest and principal discharge of the 1767 debt — with stepwise reallocation as particular debts are discharged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out precise order of payments, interest rates (1767 at 10% to 1784; Cavalry Loan at 12%; 1777 loan at 12% to Nov 1781 then 6%), and transitional distributions when loans are extinguished; apply additional Tanjore peshcush to Company's debt if prevailed upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude and punish creditors who refuse acquiescence
rubrics_metrics.description: If any creditor (Company servant or protected person) refuses to express acquiescence in these arrangements, they shall be excluded from any share of the fund, prohibited from separate measures to recover debt, and may be dismissed and sent home to England.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This encourages collective settlement and relieves the Nabob from continual importunities; refractory individuals are to be punished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbid protection to newly contracted or uninvestigated debts
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Nabob has recently contracted further debts owed to British subjects, the Company forbids any countenance or protection until the debt is fully investigated, reported home, and special instructions received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This stops extension of Company protection to potentially improper claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat prohibition on Company servants engaging in money transactions with country powers
rubrics_metrics.description: No servant of the Company, or person under its protection, shall be concerned in any loan or money transaction with country powers without the knowledge and express permission of their respective governments; violators to be sent home and denied Company protection for recoveries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition is repeated in the strongest terms and offenders are to be forthwith sent to England and punished as guilty of disobedience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay highest attention and respect to the Nabob and his family
rubrics_metrics.description: On all occasions, Company representatives are directed to pay the highest attention to the Nabob and his family; any mark of disrespect (e.g., delay in communicating peace) is reprehensible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve civility and respect to cement harmony and avert complaint.
